title: Dg resolution-square projection and its relative localization
statement:
Use cochain complexes and quasi-isomorphisms as in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and dg categories, quasi-equivalences and derived dg functor categories as in [lem-coef-dg-quasifunctor-invariance], in sufficiently large fixed universes. Let $\mathcal A$ be a dg category over $\mathbf Z$, and $\mathcal D,\mathcal E$ full dg subcategories. Let $S$ be a set of closed degree-zero arrows $s:e_s\to d_s$ with $e_s\in\mathcal E$ and $d_s\in\mathcal D$. Assume every object of $\mathcal D$ equals some $d_s$, and for every $s,t\in S$ postcomposition induces a degreewise surjective quasi-isomorphism
$$\mathcal A(e_s,e_t)\longrightarrow\mathcal A(e_s,d_t).$$
Define $\mathcal R$ to have objects $S$ and morphism complexes
$$\mathcal R(s,t)=\mathcal A(e_s,e_t)\times_{\mathcal A(e_s,d_t)}\mathcal A(d_s,d_t),$$
with the two maps postcomposition by $t$ and precomposition by $s$, differential and composition componentwise. Let $\pi:\mathcal R\to\mathcal D$ send $s$ to $d_s$ and a square $(a,b)$ to $b$. Then $\pi$ is surjective on objects and a degreewise surjective quasi-isomorphism on every morphism complex. Every closed degree-zero arrow between the projected objects lifts to a closed degree-zero square. In particular $\pi$ is a quasi-equivalence.

For any collection $W$ of closed degree-zero arrows of $\mathcal D$, put $W_{\mathcal R}=\{u:\pi(u)\in W\}$. The induced functor of enriched localizations in [lem-coef-enhanced-localization-universal]
$$\mathcal R[W_{\mathcal R}^{-1}]\longrightarrow\mathcal D[W^{-1}]$$
is an equivalence, including its induced functor and transformation objects and coherent diagram categories. The dual assertion holds for arrows $s:d_s\to e_s$ if every $d\in\mathcal D$ occurs and precomposition gives degreewise surjective quasi-isomorphisms $\mathcal A(e_s,e_t)\to\mathcal A(d_s,e_t)$: use morphism complexes $\mathcal A(d_s,d_t)\times_{\mathcal A(d_s,e_t)}\mathcal A(e_s,e_t)$ and projection to the $\mathcal D$ component.

proof.text: The pullback relation is preserved by the differentials, identities, and componentwise composition: if p_t(a)=q_s(b), then applying the differential gives the same equality because s and t are closed, and for composable pairs the two composites agree by associativity. Thus the displayed pullback complexes form a dg category and the projection pi is a dg functor. This is a direct check from the dg-category axioms and the definition of a pullback.

source.place: Proof paragraph 2; agent-formulated resolution-square construction, dg closure and composition

proof.text: Fix $s,t$ and write $X=\mathcal A(e_s,e_t)$, $Y=\mathcal A(e_s,d_t)$, $Z=\mathcal A(d_s,d_t)$, with $p:X\to Y$ postcomposition by $t$ and $q:Z\to Y$ precomposition by $s$. Put $K=\ker p$. For a cycle $k\in K^n$, injectivity of $H^n(p)$ gives $a\in X^{n-1}$ with $da=k$. Then $p(a)$ is a cycle. Surjectivity of $H^{n-1}(p)$ gives a cycle $z\in X^{n-1}$ and $v\in Y^{n-2}$ with $p(a)-p(z)=dv$. Lift $v$ to $w\in X^{n-2}$ by degreewise surjectivity. Now $a-z-dw$ lies in $K^{n-1}$ and has differential $k$. Thus every cycle of $K$ is a boundary, by the kernel/image definition of cohomology in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category].

source.place: Proof paragraph 2; agent-formulated pullback projection, kernel acyclicity

proof.text: The projection $r:X\times_Y Z\to Z$ is degreewise surjective: lift $q(b)$ under $p$ for each homogeneous $b$. Its kernel identifies with $K$ via $k\mapsto(k,0)$. If $b\in Z^n$ is closed, choose a lift $c\in(X\times_Y Z)^n$; then $dc$ is a cycle in $K^{n+1}$. Step 2 gives $h\in K^n$ with $dh=dc$, so $c-h$ is a closed lift of this very $b$. This proves surjectivity on cohomology. If a cycle $c$ has $r(c)=db$, lift $b$ to $a$ in degree $n-1$. Then $c-da$ is a cycle in $K^n$, hence equals $dk$ for $k\in K^{n-1}$, and $c=d(a+k)$. This proves injectivity on cohomology and hence the quasi-isomorphism assertion [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. The closed-lift argument with $n=0$ lifts every prescribed closed arrow between any specified pair $s,t$. The object hypothesis makes $\pi$ surjective on objects.

By the quasi-equivalence criterion in [lem-coef-dg-quasifunctor-invariance], the mapping-complex quasi-isomorphisms and object-surjectivity proved above make $\pi$ a quasi-equivalence: $H^0\pi$ is essentially surjective since every target object is literally projected. Apply the functorial derived-enrichment equivalence of [lem-coef-dg-enrichment-rectification]. Since its source inverts quasi-equivalences, the derived enrichment of $\pi$ is an enriched equivalence, with mapping objects and closed degree-zero arrows as specified there. Choose an enriched inverse $\sigma$ and coherent equivalences $\sigma\pi\simeq1_{\mathcal R}$ and $\pi\sigma\simeq1_{\mathcal D}$. We do not assert that $\sigma$ is a strict dg functor.

source.place: Proof paragraph 2; passage from the resolution-square projection to derived enriched equivalence

proof.text: Write $q_R:\mathcal R\to L_R=\mathcal R[W_{\mathcal R}^{-1}]$ and $q_D:\mathcal D\to L_D=\mathcal D[W^{-1}]$ for the enriched localizations. The functor $G=q_R\sigma$ inverts $W$: given $w:d\to d'$ in $W$, choose objects $s,t$ projecting exactly to its endpoints and a closed lift $u:s\to t$ from step 3. Then $u\in W_{\mathcal R}$. Naturality of $\sigma\pi\simeq1_{\mathcal R}$ gives $\alpha_t\circ\sigma(w)\simeq u\circ\alpha_s$. Applying $q_R$, the three other arrows are equivalences, so $G(w)$ is an equivalence. This uses this very $w$, without any saturation or conjugation-closure assumption on $W$. Also $q_D\pi$ inverts $W_{\mathcal R}$ by its definition. The enhanced functor-category universal property of [lem-coef-enhanced-localization-universal] therefore gives $\overline G:L_D\to L_R$ and $\overline\pi:L_R\to L_D$ with $\overline Gq_D\simeq q_R\sigma$ and $\overline\pi q_R\simeq q_D\pi$.

source.place: Proof paragraph 2; agent-formulated relative localization of the resolution-square projection

proof.text: Using the comparisons in step 5, restriction of $\overline G\,\overline\pi$ along $q_R$ is $\overline Gq_D\pi\simeq q_R\sigma\pi\simeq q_R$. Restriction of $\overline\pi\,\overline G$ along $q_D$ is $\overline\pi q_R\sigma\simeq q_D\pi\sigma\simeq q_D$. Fully faithful restriction on transformations and their higher homotopies in [lem-coef-enhanced-localization-universal] lifts these to $\overline G\,\overline\pi\simeq1_{L_R}$ and $\overline\pi\,\overline G\simeq1_{L_D}$. The resulting enriched inverse equivalences give inverse precomposition and postcomposition functors: whiskering the two displayed equivalences gives their unit and counit comparisons. They identify transformation objects as well, and applying them objectwise to a coherent diagram gives inverse diagram functors; the same node supplies compatibility with composition and all higher homotopies. This proves every enhanced clause.

source.place: Proof paragraph 2; enhanced functor and coherent-diagram consequences

proof.text: For $s:d_s\to e_s$ and $t:d_t\to e_t$, the square equation is $tb=as$. For each pair use $X=\mathcal A(e_s,e_t)$, $Y=\mathcal A(d_s,e_t)$, $Z=\mathcal A(d_s,d_t)$, $p(a)=as$ and $q(b)=tb$. Both are chain maps because $s,t$ are closed; the assumed precomposition map is precisely $p$. Swapping the two factors identifies the displayed dual morphism complex with $X\times_Y Z$, with projection $r$ to $Z$. The componentwise dg checks in step 1 and the cycle calculations in steps 2–3 apply verbatim to these maps. The object hypothesis again makes the projection surjective. Steps 4–6 now apply to this dg projection and any chosen $W$, proving the dual clause with the stated variance.
